newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian paper carries photo of recovering Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Russian paper carries photo of recovering Yeltsin.

text.p: A Russian newspaper on Saturday published the first picture of President Boris Yeltsin since he underwent open heart surgery and the presidential press service said the patient was doing fine.
The photograph, taking up much of the front page of the liberal daily Sevodnya, showed a relaxed-looking Yeltsin drinking tea with his wife Naina and granddaugher Masha.
Yeltsin was wearing an open-necked shirt and a patterned cardigan.

Sevodnya said the photograph, released by the presidential press service, was taken on Friday in the presidential wing of the Central Clinical Hospital, where Yeltsin is recovering from a quintuple bypass operation.
The presidential press service said in a statement that doctors had removed some of Yeltsin's stitches after his operation, aimed to improve the blood supply to his heart.
"Today, 11 days after the operation, the condition of B.N. Yeltsin is stable," said the statement, which detailed Yeltsin's pulse, blood pressure and breathing.

Yeltsin has just completed the first 100 days of his second term in office, but his heart problems meant he has only been in the Kremlin a few times. Most of his time has been spent in a complex of government rest houses outside Moscow.
The picture seemed to be the latest step in the Kremlin's strategy of gradually preparing the 65-year-old president for a full public appearance.
Kremlin press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Friday a planned address to the nation, Yeltsin's first public act, was still being prepared. But he did not say when it would be.
"You understand, the imagemakers want the president's appearance to have a big impact," he said.
Yastrzhembsky had said on Tuesday that Yeltsin would address the nation within days, but did not specify whether this would be on television or radio.
